## Purpose Resolves https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36066 For models that use QK RMSNorm (e.g. Qwen3), the post-projection path currently requires multiple kernel launches: 1. A triton kernel for Qknorm 2. A Triton kernel for RoPE 3. `reshape_and_cache_flash` for KV cache write + optional FP8 quant This PR fuses all of them into a **single CUDA kernel** (`fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant`), eliminating intermediate global memory round-trips and multiple kernel launch overheads. wo kernels and the extra kernel launch overhead. ## What's included **CUDA kernel** (`csrc/fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.cu`) - Warp-per-head design: one warp handles RMSNorm + RoPE + cache write for a single head - Supports both NeoX and GPT-J RoPE styles - Supports BF16/FP16 compute with optional FP8 KV cache quantization - Vectorized loads (vec2/vec4) and warp-shuffle RMSNorm (no shared memory) - V is written to cache first (fire-and-forget) while K normalization runs, hiding store latency **Compiler fusion pass** (`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/qk_norm_rope_cache_quant_fusion.py`) - Pattern-matches qknorm+rope+optional quant+cache write in the Inductor post-grad graph - Replaces them with a single fused op call, resolving runtime KV cache context via `layer_name` - Gated behind `CompilationConfig.fuse_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant` (default off) **Tests & benchmarks** - Standalone correctness test against the unfused baseline (`tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py`) - Kernel-level benchmark: fused vs baseline (`tests/kernels/bench_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py`) - NCU profiling harness (`tests/kernels/bench_fused_qknrc_ncu.py`) ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit test (requires GPU) python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py -v # Benchmark (fused vs baseline, various batch sizes) python tests/kernels/bench_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py # nsys # E2E data ``` ## Test Result ### Nsys Rough numbers on H20, Qwen3-4B config (32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim=128): | Batch | Unfused | Fused | Speedup | |------:|--------:|------:|--------:| | small batch| 5.0us | 2.3us | 2.17x | | middle batch | 17.0us | 12.0us | 1.42x | | large batch | 28.2us | 23.0us | 1.23x | Unfused Max Cost Unfused Min Cost Fused Max Cost Fuse Min Cost ## How to enable Not enabled by default. To opt in, set in your vLLM config: compilation_config={"pass_config": {"fuse_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant": True}} ---

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a fused CUDA kernel and a corresponding compilation pass for QK RMSNorm, RoPE, and KV cache writing with optional FP8 quantization, targeting memory-bandwidth-bound decode operations. The feedback identifies critical issues regarding the CUDA kernel's indexing of the rotary embedding cache when the rotary dimension is smaller than the head dimension, potential runtime errors in the Python fallback implementation when handling per-head weights, and the need for safer attribute access when retrieving KV cache scales to prevent compilation-time errors.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The kernel assumes that the `cos_sin_cache` has exactly `head_dim` elements per position. However, in many models, the rotary embedding is only applied to a subset of the head dimension (`rotary_dim < head_dim`). In such cases, `cos_sin_cache` will have `rotary_dim` elements per row, and indexing with `head_dim` will lead to out-of-bounds memory access or incorrect rotary values. You should pass the actual `rotary_dim` to the kernel and use it for indexing the cache.

+//
+// Fused QK RMSNorm + RoPE + KV Cache Write + FP8 Per-Tensor Quantisation
+//
+// One CUDA thread-block processes one token.
+//   Q heads:  RMSNorm → RoPE → write BF16/FP16 to q_out
+//   K heads:  RMSNorm → RoPE → FP8 quantise → write to paged k_cache
+//   V heads:  FP8 quantise → write to paged v_cache
+//
+// Build (standalone, for rapid testing):
+//   torch.utils.cpp_extension.load(
+//       name="fused_qknrc",
+//       sources=["csrc/fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.cu"],
+//       extra_cuda_cflags=["-O3", "--use_fast_math"])
+
+#include <torch/extension.h>
+#include <ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h>
+#include <c10/cuda/CUDAGuard.h>
+#include <cuda.h>
+#include <cuda_runtime.h>
+#include <cuda_fp16.h>
+#include <cuda_bf16.h>
+
+// FP8 header – available since CUDA 11.8.
+// HW-accelerated conversion requires SM >= 89 (Ada / Hopper).
+#if defined(CUDA_VERSION) && CUDA_VERSION >= 11080
+#include <cuda_fp8.h>
+#define HAS_CUDA_FP8 1
+#else
+#define HAS_CUDA_FP8 0
+#endif
+
+namespace fused_qknrc {
+
+// ── Warp / block reduction ────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+__device__ __forceinline__ float warp_reduce_sum(float val) {
+#pragma unroll
+  for (int mask = 16; mask > 0; mask >>= 1)
+    val += __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, val, mask);
+  return val;
+}
+
+// Returns the sum across the full block.  `reduce_smem` must have room for
+// at least (blockDim.x / 32) floats.
+__device__ float block_reduce_sum(float val, float* reduce_smem) {
+  const int lane = threadIdx.x & 31;
+  const int wid = threadIdx.x >> 5;
+
+  val = warp_reduce_sum(val);
+  if (lane == 0) reduce_smem[wid] = val;
+  __syncthreads();
+
+  const int num_warps = (blockDim.x + 31) >> 5;
+  val = (threadIdx.x < num_warps) ? reduce_smem[threadIdx.x] : 0.f;
+  if (wid == 0) val = warp_reduce_sum(val);
+  return val;
+}
+
+// ── FP8 E4M3 conversion helpers ──────────────────────────────────────
+
+__device__ __forceinline__ uint8_t float_to_fp8_e4m3(float val) {
+#if HAS_CUDA_FP8 && __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 890
+  return static_cast<uint8_t>(
+      __nv_cvt_float_to_fp8(val, __NV_SATFINITE, __NV_E4M3));
+#else
+  // Software fallback – saturate to E4M3 range [-448, 448], then cast
+  // through half for a rough approximation.  Good enough for correctness
+  // testing on Ampere / older GPUs.
+  val = fminf(fmaxf(val, -448.f), 448.f);
+  // Pack into unsigned byte via half roundtrip (lossy but deterministic).
+  __half h = __float2half_rn(val);
+  // Re-interpret the 16-bit pattern; truncate mantissa.
+  unsigned short bits = *reinterpret_cast<unsigned short*>(&h);
+  // Simplified E4M3: sign(1) | exp(4) | man(3)
+  uint8_t sign = (bits >> 15) & 1;
+  int exp_h = ((bits >> 10) & 0x1F) - 15;   // de-bias half exponent
+  int man_h = (bits >> 7) & 0x7;             // top 3 mantissa bits
+  int exp_fp8 = exp_h + 7;                   // re-bias for E4M3 (bias=7)
+  if (exp_fp8 <= 0) {
+    return (sign << 7);                       // ±0 / underflow
+  }
+  if (exp_fp8 >= 15) {
+    return (sign << 7) | 0x7E;               // max normal (±448)
+  }
+  return (sign << 7) | ((exp_fp8 & 0xF) << 3) | (man_h & 0x7);
+#endif

+//   IS_FP8    – true = write KV cache as FP8 E4M3, false = same as scalar_t

+    scalar_t* __restrict__ q_out,          // [T, num_heads_q * head_dim]
+    void* __restrict__ k_cache,            // NHD [B, blk_sz, nkv, hd]
+    void* __restrict__ v_cache,            // NHD [B, blk_sz, nkv, hd]
+    // ── inputs ──

+    const scalar_t* __restrict__ q_weight, // [head_dim]
+    const scalar_t* __restrict__ k_weight, // [head_dim]
+    const scalar_t* __restrict__ cos_sin_cache, // [max_pos, rot_dim]
+    const int64_t* __restrict__ positions,      // [T]
+    const int64_t* __restrict__ slot_mapping,   // [T]
+    // ── scalars ──

+    const int num_heads_q, const int num_heads_kv, const int head_dim,

+  const int tid = threadIdx.x;

+  const int kv_size = num_heads_kv * head_dim;
+  const int embed_dim = head_dim / 2;  // rotary half

+  const scalar_t* k_in = q_in + q_size;
+  const scalar_t* v_in = k_in + kv_size;

+  const scalar_t* cos_ptr = cos_sin_cache + pos * head_dim;

The implementation of `_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant_impl` assumes that `q_weight` and `k_weight` are shared across all heads by calling `.view(head_dim)`. If a model uses per-head QK normalization weights (where the weight shape is `[num_heads, head_dim]`), this call will raise a `RuntimeError` because the total number of elements won't match `head_dim`. The fusion pass should either verify that the weights are shared (broadcastable from `[head_dim]`) or the implementation should handle per-head weights correctly.

```suggestion
        weight=q_weight.view(-1, head_dim)[0] if q_weight.numel() == head_dim else q_weight.view(num_heads, head_dim),
```

## Purpose Resolves https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/36066 For models that use QK RMSNorm (e.g. Qwen3), the post-projection path currently requires multiple kernel launches: 1. A triton kernel for Qknorm 2. A Triton kernel for RoPE 3. `reshape_and_cache_flash` for KV cache write + optional FP8 quant This PR fuses all of them into a **single CUDA kernel** (`fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant`), eliminating intermediate global memory round-trips and multiple kernel launch overheads. wo kernels and the extra kernel launch overhead. ## What's included **CUDA kernel** (`csrc/fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.cu`) - Warp-per-head design: one warp handles RMSNorm + RoPE + cache write for a single head - Supports both NeoX and GPT-J RoPE styles - Supports BF16/FP16 compute with optional FP8 KV cache quantization - Vectorized loads (vec2/vec4) and warp-shuffle RMSNorm (no shared memory) - V is written to cache first (fire-and-forget) while K normalization runs, hiding store latency **Compiler fusion pass** (`vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/qk_norm_rope_cache_quant_fusion.py`) - Pattern-matches qknorm+rope+optional quant+cache write in the Inductor post-grad graph - Replaces them with a single fused op call, resolving runtime KV cache context via `layer_name` - Gated behind `CompilationConfig.fuse_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant` (default off) **Tests & benchmarks** - Standalone correctness test against the unfused baseline (`tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py`) - Kernel-level benchmark: fused vs baseline (`tests/kernels/bench_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py`) - NCU profiling harness (`tests/kernels/bench_fused_qknrc_ncu.py`) ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit test (requires GPU) python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py -v # Benchmark (fused vs baseline, various batch sizes) python tests/kernels/bench_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py # nsys # E2E data ``` ## Test Result ### Nsys Rough numbers on H20, Qwen3-4B config (32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim=128): | Batch | Unfused | Fused | Speedup | |------:|--------:|------:|--------:| | small batch| 5.0us | 2.3us | 2.17x | | middle batch | 17.0us | 12.0us | 1.42x | | large batch | 28.2us | 23.0us | 1.23x | Unfused Max Cost Unfused Min Cost Fused Max Cost Fuse Min Cost ## How to enable Not enabled by default. +"""
+Test for the fused QK RMSNorm + RoPE + KV Cache + FP8-Quant CUDA kernel.
+
+Run:
+    python tests/kernels/test_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.py

+
+import torch
+
+import vllm._C  # noqa: F401  – loads the _C extension
+
+
+# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# Reference implementation (pure PyTorch)
+# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+
+def rms_norm_ref(x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, eps: float):
+    """RMSNorm over the last dimension."""
+    variance = x.to(torch.float32).pow(2).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    x_normed = x * torch.rsqrt(variance + eps)
+    return (x_normed * weight).to(x.dtype)
+
+
+def rotary_embedding_neox_ref(
+    q: torch.Tensor,  # [T, num_heads, head_dim]
+    k: torch.Tensor,  # [T, num_kv_heads, head_dim]
+    cos: torch.Tensor,  # [T, head_dim/2]
+    sin: torch.Tensor,  # [T, head_dim/2]
+):
+    """Apply GPT-NeoX-style rotary embeddings."""
+    embed_dim = q.shape[-1] // 2
+    q_x, q_y = q[..., :embed_dim], q[..., embed_dim:]
+    k_x, k_y = k[..., :embed_dim], k[..., embed_dim:]
+
+    # Expand cos/sin for heads: [T, 1, embed_dim]
+    c = cos.unsqueeze(1)
+    s = sin.unsqueeze(1)
+
+    q_out = torch.cat([q_x * c - q_y * s, q_y * c + q_x * s], dim=-1)
+    k_out = torch.cat([k_x * c - k_y * s, k_y * c + k_x * s], dim=-1)
+    return q_out.to(q.dtype), k_out.to(k.dtype)
+

+    qkv: torch.Tensor,  # [T, (nq+2*nkv)*hd]

+    k_weight: torch.Tensor,  # [head_dim]

+    slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,  # [T]
+    k_cache: torch.Tensor,  # [num_blocks, block_size, nkv, hd]

+    epsilon: float,

+    num_heads_kv: int,
+    head_dim: int,
+    block_size: int,
+    is_fp8: bool,
+):

+    T = qkv.shape[0]
+    q_size = num_heads_q * head_dim
+    kv_size = num_heads_kv * head_dim
+
+    q_flat = qkv[:, :q_size]
+    k_flat = qkv[:, q_size : q_size + kv_size]
+    v_flat = qkv[:, q_size + kv_size :]
+
+    # Reshape to per-head
+    q_heads = q_flat.view(T, num_heads_q, head_dim)
+    k_heads = k_flat.view(T, num_heads_kv, head_dim)
+    v_heads = v_flat.view(T, num_heads_kv, head_dim)
+
+    # RMSNorm per head
+    q_normed = rms_norm_ref(q_heads.float(), q_weight.float(), epsilon).to(

+    )
+    k_normed = rms_norm_ref(k_heads.float(), k_weight.float(), epsilon).to(
+        qkv.dtype
+    )
+
+    # Gather cos/sin for each token's position
+    embed_dim = head_dim // 2
+    cos = cos_sin_cache[positions, :embed_dim].float()  # [T, embed_dim]
+    sin = cos_sin_cache[positions, embed_dim:].float()  # [T, embed_dim]

+    )
+    q_rope = q_rope.to(qkv.dtype)
+    k_rope = k_rope.to(qkv.dtype)
+
+    # Q output: flatten back
+    q_out = q_rope.view(T, q_size)
+

+            k_cache[blk, off] = k_rope[t]

The kernel assumes that the `cos_sin_cache` has exactly `head_dim` elements per position. However, in many models, the rotary embedding is only applied to a subset of the head dimension (`rotary_dim < head_dim`). In such cases, `cos_sin_cache` will have `rotary_dim` elements per row, and indexing with `head_dim` will lead to out-of-bounds memory access or incorrect rotary values. You should pass the actual `rotary_dim` to the kernel and use it for indexing the cache.

The implementation of `_fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant_impl` assumes that `q_weight` and `k_weight` are shared across all heads by calling `.view(head_dim)`. +//
+// Fused QK RMSNorm + RoPE + KV Cache Write + FP8 Per-Tensor Quantisation
+//
+// One CUDA thread-block processes one token.
+//   Q heads:  RMSNorm → RoPE → write BF16/FP16 to q_out
+//   K heads:  RMSNorm → RoPE → FP8 quantise → write to paged k_cache
+//   V heads:  FP8 quantise → write to paged v_cache
+//
+// Build (standalone, for rapid testing):
+//   torch.utils.cpp_extension.load(

+//       sources=["csrc/fused_qk_norm_rope_cache_quant.cu"],
+//       extra_cuda_cflags=["-O3", "--use_fast_math"])

+#include <ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h>
+#include <c10/cuda/CUDAGuard.h>
+#include <cuda.h>
+#include <cuda_runtime.h>
+#include <cuda_fp16.h>
+#include <cuda_bf16.h>

+#define HAS_CUDA_FP8 1
+#else
+#define HAS_CUDA_FP8 0
+#endif

+// ── Warp / block reduction ────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+__device__ __forceinline__ float warp_reduce_sum(float val) {
+#pragma unroll
+  for (int mask = 16; mask > 0; mask >>= 1)
+    val += __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, val, mask);
+  return val;
+}
+
+// Returns the sum across the full block.  `reduce_smem` must have room for
+// at least (blockDim.x / 32) floats.
+__device__ float block_reduce_sum(float val, float* reduce_smem) {
+  const int lane = threadIdx.x & 31;
+  const int wid = threadIdx.x >> 5;
+
+  val = warp_reduce_sum(val);
+  if (lane == 0) reduce_smem[wid] = val;
+  __syncthreads();
+
+  const int num_warps = (blockDim.x + 31) >> 5;
+  val = (threadIdx.x < num_warps) ? reduce_smem[threadIdx.x] : 0.f;
+  if (wid == 0) val = warp_reduce_sum(val);
+  return val;
+}

+// ── FP8 E4M3 conversion helpers ──────────────────────────────────────
+
+__device__ __forceinline__ uint8_t float_to_fp8_e4m3(float val) {
+#if HAS_CUDA_FP8 && __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 890

+  // Pack into unsigned byte via half roundtrip (lossy but deterministic).

+  // Re-interpret the 16-bit pattern; truncate mantissa.
+  unsigned short bits = *reinterpret_cast<unsigned short*>(&h);
+  // Simplified E4M3: sign(1) | exp(4) | man(3)

+  int exp_h = ((bits >> 10) & 0x1F) - 15;   // de-bias half exponent
